title: Pitch Follower
description: A light sensor sets the pitch of a buzzer: brighter light, higher note.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × light sensor (photoresistor), 1 × 4.7 kΩ resistor, 1 × piezo buzzer, and some jumper wires.
Push the light sensor in, its two legs in two different columns.
steps.goal: Put the light sensor on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. One leg of the light sensor → that same row.
steps.goal: Connect one leg of the light sensor to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the light sensor's other leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
steps.goal: Connect the light sensor's other leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Push a 4.7 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the same column as the pin A0 wire, the other leg in an empty column.
hints: The light sensor and this resistor share the 5 V between them — so the pin's voltage changes as the light sensor does.
steps.goal: Put a 4.7 kΩ resistor next to the pin A0 wire.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. That resistor's other leg → that same row.
hints: Now the reading goes up when the light gets brighter.
steps.goal: Connect the 4.7 kΩ resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push the buzzer in, its two legs in two different columns.
hints: The + leg is marked on top (and is usually longer).
It only works one way round.
steps.goal: Put the buzzer on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the buzzer's + leg to pin 9 on the Arduino.
hints: tone() on this pin makes the buzzer sing.
steps.goal: Connect the buzzer's + leg to pin 9.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the buzzer's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the buzzer's − leg to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Wave your hand over the light sensor: the note goes down when it's darker and up when it's brighter.
